Trail: Halve cross-region authz round trips on /repos/batch; stop logging client aborts as 503 outages
  Number:  419
  ID:      019f95d0-10b8-7626-b398-23c0c61f6cb4
  Branch:  combine-repo-access-bulk-check
  Base:    main
  Status:  open
  Author:  dipree
  Phase:   building
  URL:     https://entire.io/gh/entirehq/entire-api/trails/419
  Assignees: dipree
  Created: 2026-07-24T20:27:48Z
  Updated: 2026-07-24T20:46:44Z

Description:
Problem
/repos/batch (the web app's login-time repo hydration, fanned out per cell by the BFF) — unsampled Datadog logs, 24h, successful requests only:
| cell | n | P50 | P95 | |---|---|---|---| | us-east-2 | 3,348 | 151ms | 195ms | | eu-central-1 | 3,112 | 611ms | 732ms | | ap-southeast-2 | 2,884 | 48ms | 1,206ms (bimodal) | | ap-south-1 | 321 | 1,182ms | 2,967ms (max 4.2s) | | eu-west-1 | 311 | 88ms | 732ms |
The gap tracks distance from SpiceDB (us-east-2): the handler ran two sequential BulkCan rounds (RepoIDsWithPermission(ViewMetadata) then ResolveRepoAccess ids×4) — each round internally minimize_latency + a full-consistency recheck of denials — so remote cells paid up to four sequential cross-region waves. ap-south-1 (India) is the worst affected cell.
Separately: the chronic "EU/AU repos/batch 503" noise (~195/day EU) turned out to be client aborts, not server failures — the 503s die at P50 154ms (no timeout shape), line up with $pageleave events to the second, and surface as authz bulk check: rpc error: code = Canceled, which logServerErrors logged as server error response at Error level. That mislabeling sent today's blank-page investigation down a wrong path for a while.
Change
AccessChecker.VisibleRepoAccess: one BulkCan of ids×5 actions (view_metadata + pull/push/manage_settings/manage). Access facts for non-visible ids are checked and discarded — bulk items are cheap next to a cross-region round trip. Results are identical to the sequential pair (the new test proves equality and that bulk round trips strictly decrease); fail-closed identically. Expected: EU P50 611ms → ~300ms; India P50 1.18s → ~600ms.
logServerErrors: when the request context is already canceled, log request canceled by client at Warn instead of server error response at Error. The 5xx never reaches anyone (the client is gone); error-level was pure alert noise.
Follow-up candidates (not in this trail)
BulkCan's full-consistency recheck of denials runs on every public-repo page load (anon users are denied push/manage on everything) — gating that retry to grant-bearing actions would remove the second wave entirely, but changes recency semantics for fresh grants; needs a product call.
Regional SpiceDB read replicas would remove the cross-region wave for EU/AU/IN cells altogether — ap-south-1's P50 1.18s / P95 3s makes it the strongest case.

entire api — Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
Make an authenticated HTTP request to an Entire API and print the JSON response.

The CLI attaches the right bearer token and dials the right host for the
chosen backend, so you don't have to plumb auth yourself:

  --to core   the control plane (default): orgs, repos, mirrors, clusters, /me
  --to cell   your home entire-api cell: /me/* activity, repo aggregates

Use --jurisdiction <slug> (e.g. us, eu) to reach a specific jurisdiction's
entire-api cell instead of your home one; it implies --to cell.

<path> is the full path on that host, e.g. /api/v1/clusters. These
placeholders are filled from the current repo's origin remote:
  {owner} {repo}   the GitHub owner / repo
  {repo_id}        the repo's Entire ULID (from its mirror) — cells key on this

    15	// ti builds a minimal RepoAccess for byte-shape tests that don't exercise
    16	// capabilities — DataRole tracks the tier for read/write so the wire object stays
    17	// self-consistent (admin defaults to a read data role, matching a settings admin
    18	// with no git access).
    19	func ti(tier string) auth.RepoAccess {
    20		dataRole := auth.RepoTierRead
    21		if tier == auth.RepoTierWrite {
    22			dataRole = auth.RepoTierWrite
    23		}
    24		return auth.RepoAccess{Tier: tier, DataRole: dataRole, CanPull: true}
    25	}

   352	// TestMemberRepoAccess proves the discovery list scopes to the membership set
   353	// (repo/list), NOT the pull set, and that the resolved RepoAccess splits the
   354	// legacy tier from the capabilities. Since COR-904 the admin tier derives from
   355	// manage_settings (not push), so a settings admin with NO push reads admin/read;
   356	// data_role tracks push independently. A repo the caller can only pull
   357	// (public_viewer wildcard) or only manage (super-admin cascade) — but is not a
   358	// member of — is excluded, and a SpiceDB error fails closed.
   359	func TestMemberRepoAccess(t *testing.T) {
   360		ctx := context.Background()
   361		// Membership: m1 read-only, m2 writable, m3 full admin (push + manage_settings
   362		// + manage), m4 a platform-admin shape (manage_settings but NO push/manage).
   363		// pub is pullable-only (public_viewer wildcard) and cascadeAdmin is
   364		// manage_settings-only-without-membership — neither is in the membership set,
   365		// so neither may appear.
   366		reader := authz.NewReaderFromClient(&fakeAuthz{
   367			listRepos:           toSet([]string{"m1", "m2", "m3", "m4"}),
   368			repos:               toSet([]string{"m1", "m2", "m3", "m4", "pub"}), // pull set: members + a public repo
   369			pushRepos:           toSet([]string{"m2", "m3"}),
   370			manageSettingsRepos: toSet([]string{"m3", "m4", "cascadeAdmin"}), // admin tier + a non-member cascade
   371			manageRepos:         toSet([]string{"m3"}),                       // only m3 holds manage
   372		})
   373		access, err := checker(t, reader).MemberRepoAccess(ctx)
   374		if err != nil {
   375			t.Fatalf("tiers: %v", err)
   376		}
   377	
   378		want := map[string]auth.RepoAccess{
   379			// (d) reader: read / read / no settings / no manage.
   380			"m1": {Tier: "read", DataRole: "read", CanPull: true, CanManageSettings: false, HoldsManage: false},
   381			// (c) push only: write / write / no settings / no manage.
   382			"m2": {Tier: "write", DataRole: "write", CanPull: true, CanManageSettings: false, HoldsManage: false},
   383			// (a) push + manage_settings + manage: admin / write / settings / manage.
   384			"m3": {Tier: "admin", DataRole: "write", CanPull: true, CanManageSettings: true, HoldsManage: true},
   385			// (b) manage_settings only, NO push (platform-admin shape): admin / READ /
   386			//     settings / no manage.
   387			"m4": {Tier: "admin", DataRole: "read", CanPull: true, CanManageSettings: true, HoldsManage: false},
   388		}
   389		if len(access) != len(want) {

   391		}
   392		for id, w := range want {

   394				t.Errorf("%s: got %+v, want %+v", id, access[id], w)
   395			}
   396		}
   397		// The public-viewer-only and cascade-only repos must be absent — they are
   398		// pullable/manage_settings but not membership.
   399		if _, ok := access["pub"]; ok {
   400			t.Error("public-viewer repo leaked into the discovery list (should be membership-scoped)")
   401		}
   402		if _, ok := access["cascadeAdmin"]; ok {
   403			t.Error("super-admin-cascade repo leaked into the discovery list (should be membership-scoped)")
   404		}
   405	
   406		// Fail-closed: a SpiceDB error surfaces, never a partial map.
   407		if _, err := checker(t, fakeReader(nil, nil, true)).MemberRepoAccess(ctx); err == nil {
   408			t.Error("want error when SpiceDB is down, got nil")
   409		}
   410	}

### The backend issue underneath (chronic, multi-user)

At login the app fans out `POST /api/v1/repos/batch` to every cell. **EU (eu-central-1) and AU (ap-southeast-2) have been 503ing this endpoint every hour for 24+ hours** (10–22/hr in EU). The user's own 18:57:42 request is in the logs, failing with:

The frontend logs these as `ApiError: entire-api request failed` (`src/lib/api/client.ts`) — the top error-tracking issue today.

content.text:
## Verdict

**It is a real improvement for small, mostly authorized batches, but I would not merge it unchanged.** Two medium findings remain open.

### Findings

1. **`VisibleRepoAccess` can severely regress large denied batches**  
   `BulkCan` chunks at 100 checks with concurrency 4. `/repos/batch` accepts 500 arbitrary IDs:
   - Old all-denied path: 10 SpiceDB RPCs, ~4 serialized waves.
   - New path: 50 RPCs, ~14 waves.

   The new five-ID test never crosses a chunk boundary, so it does not prove the claimed general round-trip reduction. I added this finding to trail 419.

2. **Canceled context does not prove a benign client navigation**  
   `internal/httpapi/errors.go:71` demotes every canceled/deadline-exceeded request to Warn as “request canceled by client.” The server has a concrete 30-second request deadline in `router.go`, and a BFF cancellation can itself indicate backend latency exceeding its budget. Those failures would be removed from error-level outage signals.

   The existing trail finding is valid in substance, although its `WriteTimeout` example is less direct than the application timeout.

### What is good

- Authorization results, ordering, deduplication, and fail-closed behavior appear preserved.
- For common small batches, sequential authz stages generally drop from 3–4 cross-region waves to 2.
- The implementation is straightforward.
- `go test ./...` passes on the trail commit.

### Recommendation

Keep the combined path for bounded small batches, retain the visibility-first path for larger batches, and add max-size mostly/all-denied tests. Restrict log demotion to cases known to be benign, or preserve an error metric for budget/deadline cancellations.

**Overall: directionally good, but not yet an unconditional latency improvement.**

Description:
Problem
/repos/batch (the web app's login-time repo hydration, fanned out per cell by the BFF) — unsampled Datadog logs, 24h, successful requests only:
| cell | n | P50 | P95 | |---|---|---|---| | us-east-2 | 3,348 | 151ms | 195ms | | eu-central-1 | 3,112 | 611ms | 732ms | | ap-southeast-2 | 2,884 | 48ms | 1,206ms (bimodal) | | ap-south-1 | 321 | 1,182ms | 2,967ms (max 4.2s) | | eu-west-1 | 311 | 88ms | 732ms |
The gap tracks distance from SpiceDB (us-east-2): the handler ran two sequential BulkCan rounds (RepoIDsWithPermission(ViewMetadata) then ResolveRepoAccess ids×4) — each round internally minimize_latency + a full-consistency recheck of denials — so remote cells paid up to four sequential cross-region waves. ap-south-1 (India) is the worst affected cell.
Separately: the chronic "EU/AU repos/batch 503" noise (~195/day EU) turned out to be client aborts, not server failures — the 503s die at P50 154ms (no timeout shape), line up with $pageleave events to the second, and surface as authz bulk check: rpc error: code = Canceled, which logServerErrors logged as server error response at Error level. That mislabeling sent today's blank-page investigation down a wrong path for a while.
Change
AccessChecker.VisibleRepoAccess: one BulkCan of ids×5 actions (view_metadata + pull/push/manage_settings/manage). Access facts for non-visible ids are checked and discarded — bulk items are cheap next to a cross-region round trip. Results are identical to the sequential pair (the new test proves equality and that bulk round trips strictly decrease); fail-closed identically. Expected: EU P50 611ms → ~300ms; India P50 1.18s → ~600ms.
logServerErrors: when the request context is already canceled, log request canceled by client at Warn instead of server error response at Error. The 5xx never reaches anyone (the client is gone); error-level was pure alert noise.
Follow-up candidates (not in this trail)
BulkCan's full-consistency recheck of denials runs on every public-repo page load (anon users are denied push/manage on everything) — gating that retry to grant-bearing actions would remove the second wave entirely, but changes recency semantics for fresh grants; needs a product call.
Regional SpiceDB read replicas would remove the cross-region wave for EU/AU/IN cells altogether — ap-south-1's P50 1.18s / P95 3s makes it the strongest case.

Problem
/repos/batch is the web app's login-time repo hydration, fanned out per cell by the BFF. Unsampled Datadog logs over 24h showed successful-request latency tracking distance from SpiceDB in us-east-2: US P50 151ms, EU P50 611ms, and India P50 1.18s/P95 2.97s. Separately, routine browser/page-navigation aborts surfaced as authz code=Canceled 503 errors even though the client was already gone, creating chronic EU/AU outage noise.

AccessChecker.VisibleRepoAccess now uses an adaptive strategy:
- Up to 20 unique IDs: combine view_metadata + pull/push/manage_settings/manage in one BulkCan. Five facts × 20 IDs fits one 100-item SpiceDB bulk request and removes a sequential cross-region round trip.
- Larger batches: retain visibility-first filtering, then resolve facts only for survivors. This prevents stale, hostile, or all-denied max-size batches from multiplying RPCs and full-consistency retries.

Expected impact
Small per-cell hydration batches save one cross-region authz stage. Large batches remain bounded at the previous work profile rather than risking a regression. Production latency should be measured after rollout rather than assuming every request halves.

Follow-up candidates
- Revisit BulkCan's full-consistency denial retry for actions where stale denials are acceptable; this requires a product consistency decision.
- Regional SpiceDB read replicas would remove cross-region latency for EU/AU/IN cells.
EOF

- ❌ Intent/review prompt is empty
- ❌ Transcript-based summaries/search may be degraded

The original Pi file does contain user prompts, so this is likely a compatibility bug with Pi’s current v3 transcript format—not missing session data. Reattaching after the parser is fixed should restore the structured view.
Investigate in the CLI (this repo) what's wrong.

	entries, summarizeErr := summarize.BuildCondensedTranscriptFromBytes(redacted, agent.AgentTypePi)

}

I found **two independent CLI wiring bugs**. The Pi transcript itself is valid and stored correctly.

### 1. `session attach` ignores Pi’s metadata extractors

`cmd/entire/cli/attach.go:288` calls:

```go
meta := extractTranscriptMetadata(transcriptData)
```

That generic parser only understands Claude/Cursor-style top-level `type:"user"` records and Gemini JSON. Pi uses:

```json
{"type":"message","message":{"role":"user", ...}}
```

Although `PiAgent` implements both `PromptExtractor` and `ModelExtractor`, attach never calls them.

On the captured checkpoint transcript, Pi’s actual extractor returns:

- 3 user prompts
- First prompt: the trail-review request
- Model: `gpt-5.6-sol`

### 2. `checkpoint explain` never dispatches raw transcripts to the Pi compactor

`BuildCondensedTranscriptFromBytes` handles Gemini, Droid, OpenCode, and Codex explicitly, but not `AgentTypePi`. Pi therefore falls into the Claude parser and produces zero entries.

A working native Pi compactor already exists in:

```text
cmd/entire/cli/transcript/compact/pi.go
```

Testing the exact stored transcript:

```text
compact.Compact: success, 348447 bytes
BuildCondensedTranscriptFromBytes: success, 0 entries
```

So the compactor works; summarize/explain simply never calls it.

### Test gap

Current tests cover:

- Pi compaction directly
- Already-compacted Pi JSONL in summarize

They do **not** cover a raw Pi v3 transcript through attach or explain.

### Required fixes

1. Make attach augment generic metadata through `agent.PromptExtractor` and `agent.ModelExtractor`.
2. Add `AgentTypePi` dispatch in `BuildCondensedTranscriptFromBytes`, using `compact.Compact`.
3. Add raw Pi v3 regression tests for attach metadata and `checkpoint explain --full`.

The repo remains clean; I only investigated and reproduced the failures.

## Tech Stack

- Language: Go 1.26.x
- Build tool: mise, go modules
- Linting: golangci-lint

## Development

### Running Tests

```bash
mise run test
```

### Running Integration Tests

```bash
mise run test:integration
```

### Running All Tests (CI)

```bash
mise run test:ci
```

This runs unit tests, integration tests, and the E2E canary (Vogon agent) in sequence. Integration tests use the `//go:build integration` build tag and are located in `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/`.

### Running E2E Canary Tests (Vogon Agent)

The Vogon agent is a deterministic fake agent that exercises the full E2E test suite without making any API calls.

```bash
mise run test:e2e:canary           # Run all E2E tests with the Vogon agent
mise run test:e2e:canary TestFoo   # Run a specific test
```

- **Runs as part of `test:ci`** — canary failures block merges
- **No API calls, no cost** — safe to run freely, unlike real agent E2E tests
- **If a canary test fails, the bug is in the CLI or test infrastructure**, not in an agent
- Located in `e2e/vogon/` (binary) and `cmd/entire/cli/agent/vogon/` (Agent interface)
- The binary parses prompts via regex, creates/modifies/deletes files, and fires lifecycle hooks
- **IMPORTANT: When changing E2E test prompt wording**, the Vogon binary (`e2e/vogon/main.go`) parses prompts with hardcoded regexes. New phrasing may not match existing patterns — always run `mise run test:e2e:canary` after changing prompt text and fix Vogon's parsing if tests fail.

### Running E2E Tests (Only When Explicitly Requested)

**IMPORTANT: Do NOT run E2E tests proactively.** E2E tests make real API calls to agents, which consume tokens and cost money. Only run them when the user explicitly asks for E2E testing.

```bash
mise run test:e2e [filter]                          # All agents, filtered
mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code [filter]       # Claude Code only as an example here, replace `claude-code` with other agents to run tests for those agents
```

E2E tests:

- Use the `//go:build e2e` build tag
- Located in `e2e/tests/`
- See [`e2e/README.md`](e2e/README.md) for full documentation (structure, debugging, adding agents)
- Test real agent interactions (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, Pi, or Vogon creating files, committing, etc.)
- Validate checkpoint scenarios documented in `docs/architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md`
- Support multiple agents via `E2E_AGENT` env var (`claude-code`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `cursor`, `factoryai-droid`, `copilot-cli`, `pi`, `vogon`)

**Environment variables:**

- `E2E_AGENT` - Agent to test with (default: `claude-code`)
- `E2E_CLAUDE_MODEL` - Claude model to use (default: `haiku` for cost efficiency)
- `E2E_TIMEOUT` - Timeout per prompt (default: `2m`)

### Test Parallelization

**Always use `t.Parallel()` in tests.** Every top-level test function and subtest should call `t.Parallel()` unless it modifies process-global state (e.g., `os.Chdir()`).

```go
func TestFeature_Foo(t *testing.T) {
    t.Parallel()
    // ...
}

// Integration tests with TestEnv
func TestFeature_Bar(t *testing.T) {
    t.Parallel()
    env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
    // ...
}
```

**Exception:** Tests that modify process-global state cannot be parallelized. This includes `os.Chdir()`/`t.Chdir()` and `os.Setenv()`/`t.Setenv()` — Go's test framework will panic if these are used after `t.Parallel()`.

### Git in Tests

**Tests that touch git state must use an isolated temp repo — never the real repo CWD.**

Many handlers (lifecycle, strategy, hooks) resolve the git repo from CWD via `OpenRepository`, `GetGitCommonDir`, `DetectFileChanges`, etc. Without isolation, tests can create session state files, shadow branches, or other artifacts in the real `.git/` directory.

Use the `testutil` helpers:

```go
tmpDir := t.TempDir()
testutil.InitRepo(t, tmpDir)                    // git init + user config + disable GPG
testutil.WriteFile(t, tmpDir, "f.txt", "init")  // create a file
testutil.GitAdd(t, tmpDir, "f.txt")             // stage it
testutil.GitCommit(t, tmpDir, "init")           // commit (needs at least one commit for HEAD)
t.Chdir(tmpDir)                                 // redirect CWD-based git resolution
```

`testutil.InitRepo` configures `user.name`, `user.email`, and disables GPG signing — safe for CI environments without global git config.

**Prefer `testutil.InitRepo()` over direct `git.PlainInit()` in tests.** When a test in this repo needs an initialized repository, use `testutil.InitRepo(t, dir)` unless the test specifically needs lower-level initialization behavior that the helper cannot provide. Do not call `git.PlainInit()` directly and then create commits or run CLI git operations without also reproducing the helper's repo-local config.

**Do NOT** shell out to `git init`/`git commit` directly without setting user config and `--no-gpg-sign`, and **do NOT** run lifecycle/strategy handlers from the real repo CWD in tests.

### Config/Cache/Keyring Isolation in Tests

Tests must never read or write the developer's real `~/.config/entire`
(contexts.json, version_check.json), `~/.cache/entire` (nodes.json,
cluster_cores.json, api_discovery.json), or OS keychain. The developer may be
using `entire` for real while tests run.

- **Single resolver**: `internal/entireclient/userdirs` is the only place
  that resolves the per-user config dir (`userdirs.Config()`:
  `$ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR` else `~/.config/entire`) and cache dir
  (`userdirs.Cache()`: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/entire` else `~/.cache/entire`).
  Never derive these paths anywhere else.
- **In-process safety net**: `userdirs` and the `tokenstore` default backend
  detect `go test` (via `internal/testdirs`) and fall back to a throwaway
  per-process temp directory when their env override is unset. The fallback
  is shared across tests in one process — for per-test isolation still set
  `t.Setenv("ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR", t.TempDir())` and
  `tokenstore.UseFileBackendForTesting(...)`.
- **Spawned binaries are NOT covered**: `testing.Testing()` is false in a
  subprocess. The integration and e2e TestMains set `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR`,
  `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file`, `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE_PATH`, and
  `ENTIRE_TEST_AUTH_STORE_FILE` process-wide so every spawned `entire` (and
  every agent-invoked hook) inherits isolation. Any new harness that spawns
  the real binary must do the same.
- **Legacy auth store**: `auth.NewStore()` talks straight to the zalando
  keyring; packages whose tests can reach it need `keyring.MockInit()` in
  `TestMain` (see `cmd/entire/cli/global_test.go`) — the `testdirs` fallback
  does not cover it in-process.

### Spawning subprocesses in tests (TTY detection)

Tests that spawn the real `entire` or `git` binary need the child to be non-interactive so prompts don't hang on a developer terminal.

`interactive.CanPromptInteractively()` resolves in this order:

1. `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1` → force interactive ON (any other non-empty value → force OFF).
2. `testing.Testing()` → false. In-process `go test` runs are non-interactive by default; no per-test `t.Setenv("ENTIRE_TEST_TTY", "0")` is needed.
3. Agent sentinels (`GEMINI_CLI`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `PI_CODING_AGENT`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`) → false.
4. `CI=<non-empty-non-false>` → false.
5. `/dev/tty` probe.

For subprocesses spawning the real `entire` binary (e2e, integration tests, `entire` calling itself from a hook), prefer `execx.NonInteractive` over env-var plumbing:

```go
import "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/execx"

cmd := execx.NonInteractive(ctx, getTestBinary(), "status")
cmd.Dir = repoDir
out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
```

`execx.NonInteractive` puts the child in a new session with no controlling terminal (`Setsid` on Unix, `DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` on Windows), so the child's `/dev/tty` probe fails naturally. No env var required.

`interactive.UnderTest()` returns true when `testing.Testing()` or `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY` is set — use it where code needs to skip a real-terminal operation even if `CanPromptInteractively()` returns true (e.g., reading from `/dev/tty` directly inside `askConfirmTTY`).

### Linting and Formatting

```bash
mise run fmt && mise run lint
```

`mise run fmt` can rewrite files. Treat `mise run fmt && mise run lint` as a single verification sequence: if formatting changes anything, run lint again on the formatted tree rather than assuming a previous lint result still applies.

### Before Every Commit (REQUIRED)

**CI will fail if you skip these steps:**

```bash
mise run check
```

Equivalent expanded form:

```bash
mise run fmt      # Format code (CI enforces gofmt)
mise run lint     # Lint check (CI enforces golangci-lint)
mise run test:ci  # Run all tests (unit + integration)
```

`mise run check` runs the three commands above.

Safety note: do not treat a clean `mise run lint` result as final unless it was run after the most recent `mise run fmt` pass.

### Before Any Push Or Remote Code Update (REQUIRED)

Before pushing commits or otherwise sending code changes to any remote, run `mise run lint` on the current tree and ensure it passes. If `mise run fmt` changed files, rerun `mise run lint` on the formatted tree before pushing.

**Common CI failures from skipping this:**

- `gofmt` formatting differences → run `mise run fmt`
- Lint errors → run `mise run lint` and fix issues
- Test failures → run `mise run test` and fix

### Code Duplication Prevention

Before implementing Go code, use `/go:discover-related` to find existing utilities and patterns that might be reusable.

**Check for duplication:**

```bash
mise run dup           # Comprehensive check (threshold 50) with summary
mise run dup:staged    # Check only staged files
mise run lint          # Normal lint includes dupl at threshold 75 (new issues only)
mise run lint:full     # All issues at threshold 75
```

**Tiered thresholds:**

- **75 tokens** (lint/CI) - Blocks on serious duplication (~20+ lines)
- **50 tokens** (dup) - Advisory, catches smaller patterns (~10+ lines)

When duplication is found:

1. Check if a helper already exists in `common.go` or nearby utility files
2. If not, consider extracting the duplicated logic to a shared helper
3. If duplication is intentional (e.g., test setup), add a `//nolint:dupl` comment with explanation

Problem
`entire session attach --agent pi` stored the raw Pi transcript but emitted an empty-prompt warning and wrote no prompt/model metadata. `entire checkpoint explain --full` then reported `(failed to parse transcript)` for the same valid checkpoint.

Root causes
- Attach always used the generic Claude/Cursor/Gemini metadata parser and never called Pi's existing PromptExtractor or ModelExtractor capabilities.
- Transcript summarization had no AgentTypePi dispatch, so raw Pi v3 JSONL fell through to the Claude parser instead of the existing Pi compactor.

Change
- Augment attach metadata with agent-native prompt/model extractors when available.
- Route native Pi transcripts through the Pi compactor while retaining support for already-compacted Pi JSONL.
- Add raw Pi v3 regression coverage for attach metadata, summarization, and explain rendering.

Validation
The previously affected checkpoint now renders 103 condensed transcript entries and all three user prompts. `mise run fmt`, `mise run lint`, and `mise run test` pass (8,379 tests, 5 skipped).

Description:
Problem entire session attach --agent pi stored the raw Pi transcript but emitted an empty-prompt warning and wrote no prompt/model metadata. entire checkpoint explain --full then reported (failed to parse transcript) for the same valid checkpoint.
Root causes
Attach always used the generic Claude/Cursor/Gemini metadata parser and never called Pi's existing PromptExtractor or ModelExtractor capabilities.
Transcript summarization had no AgentTypePi dispatch, so raw Pi v3 JSONL fell through to the Claude parser instead of the existing Pi compactor.
Change
Augment attach metadata with agent-native prompt/model extractors when available.
Route native Pi transcripts through the Pi compactor while retaining support for already-compacted Pi JSONL.
Add raw Pi v3 regression coverage for attach metadata, summarization, and explain rendering.
Validation The previously affected checkpoint now renders 103 condensed transcript entries and all three user prompts. mise run fmt, mise run lint, and mise run test pass (8,379 tests, 5 skipped).

Description:
Problem entire session attach --agent pi stored the raw Pi transcript but emitted an empty-prompt warning and wrote no prompt/model metadata. entire checkpoint explain --full then reported (failed to parse transcript) for the same valid checkpoint.
Root causes
Attach always used the generic Claude/Cursor/Gemini metadata parser and never called Pi's existing PromptExtractor or ModelExtractor capabilities.
Transcript summarization had no AgentTypePi dispatch, so raw Pi v3 JSONL fell through to the Claude parser instead of the existing Pi compactor.
Change
Augment attach metadata with agent-native prompt/model extractors when available.
Route native Pi transcripts through the Pi compactor while retaining support for already-compacted Pi JSONL.
Add raw Pi v3 regression coverage for attach metadata, summarization, and explain rendering.
Validation The previously affected checkpoint now renders 103 condensed transcript entries and all three user prompts. mise run fmt, mise run lint, and mise run test pass (8,379 tests, 5 skipped).
